## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `efee2d5bde62b76350be5a1b763ae18622fc49f1`
Local-runs: none

The inputs were card objectui#11079 (body; triage `5888963850`; claim `5890776280`; os-dev-report `5891523619`), PR objectui#11109 (body, the 9-file list, the net diff against `main` at `5b2ea1757`), and the head's check-runs, read with `filter=latest` and polled to completion at 13:51Z. Check-runs on the head are 43 rows against `total_count` 43, zero `in_progress`, 40 `success`, 3 conditionally `skipped` (`Test (coverage)`, its shard-matrix row, `dependabot`). Every `Test (shard n/8)`, the `Test` roll-up, `Test (dist pins)`, `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Claim Re-read`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, the doc and citation gates and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are `success`. For context I read at the head: `renderer.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `package.json`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `skills/objectui/rules/styling.md`, `timeline-gantt-unusable-date-range.test.tsx`, the catalog producer JSON and `packages/types/src/data-display.ts`; `renderer.tsx` at the base; and, as ① asks, objectui#6750's own record (body, triage `5460854027`, report `5461061243`, ACCEPT `5461194837`).

### ① Derived judgments

Judged against triage `5888963850`: one continuous axis `[start of the first unit, end of the last unit)`, each header as wide as its unit's real length, each bar measured on the same axis, no second construction, the objectui#10866 slice-3 pins re-derived not patched, pins for all six scales plus a 28/31-day `month` case.

1. **One axis, one placement — right.** The module-private `timelineAxis(scale, min, max, locale, t)` returns `{ start, end, units[{ start, end, label }] }`, and `placeOnAxis(axis, start, end)` returns `{ start, width }` as percentages of `axis.end - axis.start`. The header cells map `axis.units` and take `placeOnAxis(axis, unit.start, unit.end).width`; `calculateBarDimensions(startDate, endDate, axis)` is one `placeOnAxis` call over two `readGanttDate` timestamps; `generateTimeScaleHeaders` is `timelineAxis(...).units.map(label)`. No bucket-index path exists anywhere in the diff: the six per-scale tables (`floor` / `step` / `label`) define what a unit is, not a second geometry. The walk (`cursor = floor(min)`, loop while the cursor is at or before `max`, push `[cursor, step(cursor))`) runs at least once whenever `min` is at or before `max`, so the span is never zero.

2. **Unit snapping — right; it is the direction's own definition.** `[start of the first unit, end of the last unit)` makes the first unit the one that CONTAINS `minDate` and the last the one that contains `maxDate`. A Jan 15 to Apr 10 month axis therefore has an April column (Apr 10 lies in April), and a Jan 31 start floors to Jan 1 so `setMonth(+1)` lands on Feb 1 instead of rolling Jan 31 into March 3. `quarter` and `year` already snapped on the base (`setMonth(Math.floor(m / 3) * 3, 1)`, `setMonth(0, 1)`); the diff extends the same rule to `hour`, `day` and `month`, and gives `week` a local-midnight floor while keeping its "Week N from the first day" count, which no spec key contradicts. Labels for a range that starts on a unit boundary are byte-identical to the base (the pinned three-month cases and #6750's six degenerate-range labels are re-pinned green).

3. **Removal of objectui#6750's `totalDuration === 0` guard — right, inside the direction, and #6750's own record says why.** Its report and ACCEPT (`5461061243`, `5461194837`) give the guard's reason: on a zero-wide min-to-max span both divisions were `0 / 0`, the CSSOM rejected `left: NaN%; width: NaN%`, and the bar rendered with no `style` at all — a SILENT failure. `{ start: 0, width: 100 }` was "that answer written down" for an axis that had no width, on the premise the base comment states: "On a zero-width axis every task covers the whole of it, by definition". Under the direction that premise cannot hold: a `minDate === maxDate` range is exactly one whole unit (May 2024 is 31 days wide), so the span is never zero and `NaN` is unreachable by construction, which the head's `calculateBarDimensions` docblock records. Keeping a `{ 0, 100 }` special case would be a bar NOT measured on the axis, the second construction triage forbids. The user-visible consequence is bounded and pre-existing in kind: a zero-length task on any plan with two distinct dates already drew `width: 0%` on the base (duration 0 over a non-zero span); only the plan whose sole dates are one same-day task moves, from a full-width bar to `left: 0%; width: 0%`. It is declared in the changeset's last bullet, the PR's Acceptance notes and deviation 2, and pin 5b now holds the new geometry with its derivation. #6750's scope split (triage `5460854027`) withheld only "what an empty gantt should look like"; a zero-length task's minimum or milestone width is a product question nobody has ruled, and it is the dev's out-of-scope finding (③ 8), not this diff's to decide.

4. **Slice-3 pins re-derived, not patched — right.** Every moved number in the six test files carries a day-count derivation comment, and most are written as the formula (`${(1 / 3) * 100}%`, `share(31, 121)`, `24 / 72`, `21 / 72`, `36 / 72`). Spot-checked by hand: 31/91 = 34.065934065934066, 59/91 = 64.83516483516483, 30/91 = 32.967032967032964, 14/91 = 15.384615384615385; the pinned-February overhangs -17/29 = -58.620689655172406 and 31/29 = 106.89655172413792, -31/29 and 60/29; 1970-01-01 to 2024-02-01 is 19754 days and the epoch bar sits at 19723/19754 = 99.84306975802369; the west and east `PINNED_MIXED` instant bar keeps its 21 h and 36 h starts and 6 h length, now over 72 h instead of 48 h. The zone-rule assertions (axis labels, tooltips, refusals) are untouched, and the zone driver's PINS list correctly needed no change.

5. **Six-scale pins plus the 28/31 `month` case — right.** `TimelineGantt.oneAxis-11079.test.tsx` runs `it.each` over `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter`, `year` on a pinned three-unit range: the second bar's `left` equals the first header's `width` as a string, its `width` equals the second header's, the last bar's `left + width` is 100 to ten places, the columns sum to 100, and the non-uniform scales pin their lengths (31/28/31, 90/91/92, 366/365/365). January to February 2026 gives 31/90 and 28/90. The card's own Oct 5 to 7 computed axis pins the Oct 6 bar at one third, not 50%. The named producer is read from disk: 31/121, 29/121, 31/121, 30/121, Implementation on the Feb header, QA Phase on the Mar header. A driven Los Angeles DST case (24/71, 23/71, 24/71, the bar on its 23-hour column) sits in the zone file.

6. **Inline percentage `width` on the header cells — right; runtime geometry is outside the ban as the rule itself states it.** AGENTS.md §2: "No inline styles (`style={{}}`), CSS Modules, or styled-components. The hazard the ban exists to stop: an inline value that hard-codes a colour, so dark mode renders identically and the design system loses theme control", and its carve-out ends "Colour only — layout, spacing and sizing stay on utilities. Full rule and worked example: `skills/objectui/rules/styling.md`." That page says the deciding property is "any inline style that hard-codes a colour such that dark mode renders identically. That last one is the property that actually decides a case — not whether the word `style` appears in the diff", and then: "a runtime geometry value (a computed bar offset, a virtualiser's row height) is a separate question this carve-out does not answer." A per-render percentage that depends on the data (31/121) cannot be a static utility, carries no colour and leaves theme control untouched; it is the same kind of value as `TimelineGanttBar`'s existing inline `left` / `width`, which the base pins already read off the style attribute (`left: 0%; width: 33.33333333333333%;`). The dev flagged it (deviation 4) rather than hid it. The styling page's open question, a stated rule for runtime geometry, is real and is escalated in ③ 4; it is not this card's.

7. **The `plugin-timeline.mdx` sentence, outside the claimed surface — right under AGENTS.md #2** ("Docs-driven. For every feature/refactor, update package `README.md` and `content/docs/...`. Not done until docs reflect the code."). The package README has no axis description (its Gantt section lists the primitives and points at the source), so the docs page is the only prose that describes the axis, and the added sentence is faithful to the diff: one axis, the first unit's start to the last unit's end, header width equal to unit length, a bar under the header of the unit it starts in. Nit, not a finding: "hour, day and week columns are equal" omits the 23- or 25-hour DST day that the changeset and the zone pin both state; a one-clause caveat would close it.

8. **Accept set and public surface.** No accepted input moves: the same `readGanttDate` read, the same `findUnusableGanttDate` refusal of unparseable row AND pinned dates by name (#6759 pin 3 covers both pinned ends), the same six scales with `month` as the unknown-scale default. The inverted-range refusal is now `if (!axis)` (deviation 3): `timelineAxis` returns `undefined` on exactly the conditions the removed test made, a NaN end or a start after the end on `readGanttDate` timestamps, and because unparseable ends are already refused above by name, what reaches it is inverted, so the `inverted` diagnostic cannot be mislabeled; #6759 pins 2, 3 and 7 are unchanged and green. `calculateBarDimensions` changed signature but is module-private, as are `timelineAxis` and `placeOnAxis`; `generateTimeScaleHeaders` keeps its exported signature (②). The header cell's classes move from `flex-1` to `shrink-0 min-w-0 overflow-hidden`: the plugin's pins select `.border-r.text-xs.font-medium.text-center`, the CI farm is green on the head so no pin on `.flex-1` survives, and under Tailwind's border-box preflight the padded, bordered cells still tile to 100%.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/11079-timeline-one-axis.md`: `'@object-ui/plugin-timeline': patch`, one package, the one versioned package the diff touches (`content/docs` and the changeset carry no version). `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Claim Re-read` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are `success` on the head. Its four bullets name every user-visible move, the label change and the same-day-plan bar included.

`Clause-②: no` — right, with the export named. `index.tsx` does `export * from './renderer'` and `package.json` exposes only `.`, so `generateTimeScaleHeaders(scale, minDate, maxDate, locale, t): string[]` IS a public export of `@object-ui/plugin-timeline`. Its name, parameter list, defaults and return type are unchanged, and its documented meaning is unchanged: "Gantt header labels for one scale across [minDate, maxDate]", exported, its docblock says, "for the spec-parity test"; the README does not document it. What moves is its VALUE for ranges the base mis-bucketed: an end inside a unit the base never emitted (Jan 15 to Apr 10 lost April) or a start that rolled over a short month (Jan 31 skipped February). Those outputs contradicted the function's own description, so correcting them is a bug fix on an existing surface, not a contract added, removed or re-typed: `patch` is the right level, and the changeset says it in words ("`generateTimeScaleHeaders`, which the package exports, returns these labels"). The callers I read are the renderer's gantt branch (now through `timelineAxis`), the spec-parity test the docblock names, and the pins the diff re-derives; a consumer outside this repository that pinned the old labels for an off-boundary range would see its pin move, and a patch note is the right notice for that.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none. The seven deviations and the one out-of-scope finding, each answered:

1. mdx sentence outside the claimed surface — answered in ① 7: required by AGENTS.md #2, faithful; DST nit only.
2. #6750 guard removed, pin 5b moves to a zero-width bar — answered in ① 3: inside the direction, declared three times; the residual product question is item 8 below.
3. Inverted-range guard folded into `if (!axis)` — answered in ① 8: the same read; the diagnostic cannot be mislabeled because unparseable ends are refused by name first; #6759 pins unchanged.
4. Inline header `width` — answered in ① 6: outside the colour ban as the rule states it. Escalated, not blocking: `styling.md` leaves runtime geometry "a separate question this carve-out does not answer", and two sites in one renderer now rely on the same reading, so the seat may ask the page's owner for one stated line.
5. Zone 2 falsified in part; `timeline-gantt-null-date-6770` and `timeline-gantt-date-type-rule-6781` moved though the dispatch did not list them — both inside the claimed `__tests__` surface, both re-derivations of the same three-bar geometry with the derivation comment. Accepted.
6. Commit trailer and PR footer form — no contract bearing; noted.
7. The PR body's "#2" autolinking to objectui issue 2 — cosmetic; the seat may rewrite it to "AGENTS.md rule 2" when it flips ready.
8. **Out-of-scope finding, confirmed: a pre-existing read-rule question, not introduced by this diff.** `readGanttDate` (head `:104`, untouched by the diff) reads a string through `toDisplayDate`, and its docblock and the mdx (line 343) both state the rule: "a date-only `2026-10-05` is local midnight of the day it names", for an END as for a start. So a producer that writes inclusive date-only ends (the catalog's API Design `2024-01-01` to `2024-01-31`, QA Phase to `2024-04-30`) gets a bar that stops at the START of its last day. On the base this was masked, not absent: equal-width columns put the Feb header at 25%, and API Design's 30 days over the 120-day min-to-max span landed at exactly 25% only because 30/120 is 1/4; Implementation, at 31/120, already sat 0.83% off its header, which is this card. On the head the true 1/121 gap shows.
